Title: Significant Otter: Tap your Apple Watch to share your mood with your partner 💑 | Product Hunt
# Significant Otter. ## Tap your Apple Watch to share your mood with your partner 💑. Simple app that reads your ❤ heart rate to generate a cute otter representing you. Tap to send your otter to your significant other. It's like a friendship bracelet meets a mood ring on your Apple Watch. No reviews yetBe the first to leave a review for Significant Otter. We started by wondering how one could use the Apple Watch beyond fitness tracking, and to support social connection. We created this simple app for couples to be in touch "from the heart," watch to watch. The app generates a cute animation representing what it infers you're doing/feeling. You can then can tap to send to one (and only one) person. It's still experimental, but would be great to hear what you think! It's available only in the US for now. @andresmh The original THREE ways to use Apple Watch. Apple Watch was always desired for "From the Heart" people just stopped focusing on that side of it. Thank you for brining it back to some many who may have forgotten about why we use tech in the first place, love. The idea is simple and great! Because Apple Store gave me This App Is Not Available To Your Store error. Looks like a few people have had the same problem: Geo locked to the US App store. It's actually an iPhone app because Apple does not have watch-only apps yet. The iPhone-only experience works, but it's really optimized for the watch experience. @vladzima @anna\_0x The app uses Apple Health data (e.g., heart rate) to generate the animation on the device (not on the cloud). Still, the rules on how to deal with that type of data in different geographies seemed complex enough to lead us to keep it US-only for now. You can open it to Russian store, I can assure you nobody will care about a heart rate data ;). @vladzima @andresmh well, if Apple Health itself is available on every country, then I see no reason why your app cannot 😉 You said yourself that the user's heart rate does not leave the device anyway.
